original_value:
Face2Face
            is an approach for real-time facial reenactment of a monocular target video sequence (e.g., Youtube video). The source sequence is also a monocular video stream, captured live with a commodity webcam. Our goal is to animate the facial expressions of the target video by a source actor and re-render the manipulated output video in a photo-realistic fashion. To this end, we first address the under-constrained problem of facial identity recovery from monocular video by non-rigid model-based bundling. At run time, we track facial expressions of both source and target video using a dense photometric consistency measure. Reenactment is then achieved by fast and efficient deformation transfer between source and target. The mouth interior that best matches the re-targeted expression is retrieved from the target sequence and warped to produce an accurate fit. Finally, we convincingly re-render the synthesized target face on top of the corresponding video stream such that it seamlessly blends with the real-world illumination. We demonstrate our method in a live setup, where Youtube videos are reenacted in real time. This live setup has also been shown at SIGGRAPH Emerging Technologies 2016, by Thies et al. where it won the Best in Show Award.

The source sequence is likewise a monocular video stream captured live with a commodity webcam. The aim is to animate the target video’s facial expressions using a source actor and then re-render the altered output in a photorealistic manner. To do so, the method first tackles the underconstrained problem of recovering facial identity from monocular video via non-rigid model-based bundling. At runtime, it tracks the facial expressions of both source and target videos with a dense photometric consistency measure. Reenactment is then performed through fast, efficient deformation transfer between source and target. The mouth interior that best fits the retargeted expression is taken from the target sequence and warped for an accurate match. Finally, the synthesized target face is convincingly re-rendered over the corresponding video stream so it blends seamlessly with the real-world illumination. The method is demonstrated in a live setup, where YouTube videos are reenacted in real time. This live setup was also shown at SIGGRAPH Emerging Technologies 2016 by Thies et al., where it received the Best in Show Award.
